message.content: In domestic cats and many other felids, the presence of a mane (the long, shaggy hair that grows around the head and neck) is controlled by a dominant allele. In lions, the same principle applies: the gene that triggers mane growth in males is dominant over the allele that would produce a “mane‑less” phenotype. Thus, if a lion inherits the dominant allele from either parent, it will develop a mane (though the size and density of the mane can still vary).
